In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of intestinal glucose and fructose absorption.
the molecular basis of nutrient transport and its regulation by intracellular signalling pathways.
understanding how the intestinal epithelium adapts to the nutritional environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fructose uptake is mediated by GLUT5 and GLUT5 and SLC5A8 (SGLT1) in the proximal small intestine, whereas GLUT5 and GLUT 2 in the small intestine and colon mediate the uptake of fructose.
the p38 MAPK pathway is involved in fructose transport, but only when it is stimulated.
the ERK and p38 pathways are involved in the regulation of GLUT5 and/or GLUT2 activity, and that the ERK, and possibly the PI 3- kinases, are involved in regulating the levels of GLUT5 and/ or GLUT2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GLUT2 levels and activity, and GLUT2 and GLUT5 trafficking, are regulated by insulin, glucose, glucagon-like peptide-1 and leptin.
the p38 pathway is a key regulator of GLUT2 trafficking, whereas the ERK pathway regulates both GLUT2 trafficking and GLUT5 intrinsic activity.
fructose transport is regulated by the p38 pathway, which is restrained by the ERK pathway, which is in turn activated by PI 3- kinase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ERK, PI 3- kinase and p38 signalling pathways are all intimately involved in the regulation of GLUT5 and/or GLUT2 levels and activity.

there are multiple intracellular signalling pathways that are capable of regulating the levels and activity of the GLUT5 and GLUT 2 transporters that mediate intestinal brush-border fructos transport.
the ERK, PI 3- kinase, and p38 pathways interact with each other to regulate the expression and intrinsic activity of GLUT5 and, to a lesser extent, GLUT2.
